questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience Japanese culture and society first-hand, and an exchange program seemed the obvious choice to be able to do this.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, no difficulty at all.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: All assistance that was required, as carefully constructed guides were given to us students by the faculty.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy. If studying at Ritsumeikan University, and if you wish to live alone, I recommend living at the Freepia Narutaki apartments. They are affordable and close to campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's quite easy, but you do have to do quite a lot of things on your own, whereas students living in dorms do receive help from the dorm staff in regards to some administrative and bureaucratic processes that you have to complete as a exchange student in Japan.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was much like process at UCPH, there was a course catalogue and you got to choose different courses, and apply to them online, where you had to choice in order of your own priority.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could contact SKP staff if you needed any help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all my desired courses, so very successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for the fact that course catalogues can change quite a bit from one semester to the other, so keep an open mind if you see that the courses available in your given semester, are quite different from the ones that you choice in the preliminary round based on course catalogues from prior semesters.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the courses quite easy compared to courses at UCPH, and course load was not heavy during the semester. However, as a minimum of 7 courses are required to keep the student visa, exam season is quite busy as you most complete more exams and written assignments than at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were no lectures as we are used to, only seminar classes (which were called lectures, but were not lectures as we are used to at UCPH).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all the courses I took.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not really an unexpected cost, but you are required by law to register in Japanese health insurance, in insurance at the faculty (includes fire insurance and house insurance, regardless of whether you live in a dorm or in housing you found on your own), so keep that in mind. Also, if you take public transport often, which most people will, it will eventually stack up and become somewhat expensive, so I recommend getting Suica or ICOCA (transport cards used in public transport, Suica is practical cause it can be used all over Japan, whilst others are more regional), and therefore you can check how much money you use on transport (if you have an iPhone, all Japanese transport cards, or IC cards as they are called, are available in Apple Wallet, if you don't want a physical card, and you can top the card up using Apple Pay).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out is quite affordable with a Danish income. Also once you are a member of the Japanese Health Insurance, it will pay for 70% of medical bills, and will pay for most medicines if needed, so there is no need for a ridiculously expensive health insurance from back home.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many, but for most a level of Japanese was required, so keep that in mind.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Honestly, whatever interests the given student. For me, I mostly interacted with Japanese friends outside of school and managed to make friendships that way, but I think some of the clubs more open to exchange students, like the English Language Club, could be fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Kyoto is a beautiful city, there is so much beautiful nature and cultural heritage to see. There is a Temple or a Jinja (Japanese Shinto Shrine) at practically every corner, so that is something I recommend doing. Also, the Kansai Region where Kyoto is located, is very beautiful and extremely diverse, and daytrips to Uji, Nara, Osaka, Ine and more are very fun activities that can be done on weekends and days off.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: For me it was quite easy, I picked up Japanese very quickly, and so being able to communicate with locals helped. There are many social rules in Japan that are deeply engrained in society and that people participate in as second nature, so in the beginning it can be difficult to catch unto all of them, but mostly people are very kind and if you do something very wrong, people will be sure to let you know. Also, given Japan is a massive tourist spot, for most things there will be English-language plaques telling you what to do and what not to do.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If you speak Japanese, even just slightly conversational, it will definitely make things easier socially, as it will help Japanese students feel more comfortable. Otherwise my biggest piece of advice is not to force social interaction, if it happens organically it will, if not then that's just the reality of it.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: i was quite at ease, no difficulties.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It was very orderly and very clean, quite easy to quickly pick up how the different systems worked.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Understand that it's a completely different academic culture from UCPH, and therefore it can be frustrating if you expect the two to be similar.  However, if you keep an open mind, it will be enjoyable. 

2. You are required to attend 75% of classes and attendance is taken during every class, it is mandatory to attend those 75% of classes otherwise you will be failed automatically. In simpler terms, for every course, you are only allowed to miss 4 classes (and that's only if you are never late to any of the other classes, as points are deducted from attendance for being late as well). I say this because many choose Japan as a destination, because they want to travel this beautiful country, but keep in mind that at Ritsumeikan, you are a student first and foremost, and you will not be able to just skip class for a week to travel around Japan as you wish. Coordinate your schedule so you have days off, and can enjoy travel, but keep in mind in regards to attendance it's quite different than what most faculties at UCPH require in terms of attendance. 

3. There will be a lot of bureaucratic processes you are required to complete when you arrive in Japan and when you leave. These are not optional, they are mandatory. The faculty will provide you with most information, but it is important that you complete all of it by the deadlines set.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think I summed it up quite well in the above answered.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the Japanese friends I made, I was really lucky to make amazing friendships and experience so many wonderful moments.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I really had none, from beginning to end it was a really good experience.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
